description: Bounded Algorithm 3.1 Delaunay-pruning kernel with r=1.

source.title: There Are Planar Graphs Almost as Good as the Complete Graphs and Almost as Cheap as Minimum Spanning Trees

input.edge_rule: 0 <= u < v < n; unique edges sorted lexicographically
input.delaunay_prerequisite: The supplied edge set must equal the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation. Duplicate points, any collinear triple, and any cocircular quadruple are invalid.

contract.starting_graph: Euclidean MST of the supplied Delaunay edges, sorted by (squared_length,u,v) for deterministic Kruskal ties
contract.contour: Double each MST edge into a directed embedded-tree contour; start at the lexicographically smallest directed dart and follow clockwise successor at each target
contract.rotation_order: Counterclockwise by exact integer half-plane and cross-product comparison
contract.stack_order: Initial eligible darts are pushed in canonical contour order. After replacing a two-edge boundary path, push the right exposed candidate first and the left candidate second; LIFO processes the left candidate first. Re-anchor the cyclic contour at its smallest dart after each replacement.
contract.shortcut_rule: Keep chord (v,u) iff accumulated boundary path weight is strictly greater than 2*EuclideanLength(v,u); otherwise carry the accumulated weight on that oriented boundary chord
contract.floating_point: Binary64 square root per edge; path weights are summed left-to-right; strict greater-than comparison, with no epsilon
contract.output: [absorbed_face_count,retained_shortcut_count,edge_count,(u,v)*edge_count] with unique retained edges sorted lexicographically

output.error_precedence: Input and Delaunay validation precede output pointer and capacity checks.

workspace.meaning: Bounded point coordinates, Delaunay edge/face tables, rotations, Kruskal state, directed contour, stack events, staged edge list, and output bytes.

references.primary: primary_oracle.py: triangle-corner LIFO stack and directed contour weights
references.independent: independent_oracle.py: face-event stack and direct exposed-boundary scan
